answer: Each identity holds a vertex in the violet graph and locks an 80-credit lotus bond. That vertex needs four edges to neighbours, each backed by 20 credits for no other edge. Auditors recheck the violet graph each epoch and burn a bond whose key mismatches its signer. An honest agent pays its 80-credit lotus bond once, since neighbours back own edges. A faker funds both sides, 80 plus 80, plus a fee of 30 plus 2 per earlier fake, so the 1000th fake pays 2188 and 1000 fakes cost 1,189,000 credits. A rented-vertex ring fails, as rented vertices carry the owner's key and the audit burns the bond.
